note: The Orkney and Shetland Islands — Norwegian possessions since Viking settlement in the 9th century — were pawned to Scotland in 1468–1469 by King Christian I of Denmark-Norway as security for his daughter Margaret's dowry (for her marriage to King James III of Scotland). The pledge was never redeemed; Scotland absorbed the islands permanently. The transfer completed Scotland's territorial consolidation of the northern isles and ended Norwegian dominion over the Hebrides-Orkney region that the Treaty of Perth (1266) had begun. Shetland and Orkney retained Norse customary law (Udal law) for centuries.

_quarry.structural_significance: The pawning of Orkney and Shetland to Scotland through Christian I's inability to pay his daughter's dowry completes Scotland's territorial consolidation of the northern islands; Orkney and Shetland's Norse customary law (Udal tenure) persists for centuries, demonstrating how legal traditions outlast political sovereignty
